The test image shows a corn ear with significant rot. Key features:
- White/pink-reddish mold growth covering much of the ear
- Tip of ear shows brown decay
- Some kernels visible with discoloration (yellow/orange)
- Pinkish-red coloration suggests fungal ear rot

Top candidates: Gibberella_Disease (pink mold starting at tip), Fusarium_Disease (white-pink scattered mold), Diplodia_Ear_Rot (white mold)

Let me check reference images one at a time, starting with Gibberella.

I've used all 16 reference views. Let me analyze the findings:

**Test image observations:**
- Corn ear still on plant, partially husked/exposed
- White/pink-reddish mold covering the ear, especially at the tip area
- Brown decay at the tip of the ear
- Some yellow/orange kernels remaining in the middle section
- Reddish-pink coloration visible on surrounding leaf tissue

**Reference comparison summary:**
- **Gibberella_Disease**: Refs 12 and 64 show pink/red kernel discoloration and pink staining on husks — closely matches the pink-reddish mold color and tip-progressing pattern in the test image
- **Fusarium_Disease**: Refs 25 and 42 show scattered white mold on individual kernels — doesn't match the more widespread, pink-tinted mold in the test image
- **Diplodia_Ear_Rot**: Ref 27 shows fallen ears, more straw-colored/white mold — pattern doesn't match
- **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**: Olive-green mold — clearly doesn't match
- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot**: Blue-green mold — clearly doesn't match
- **Common_Smut**: Black galls — clearly doesn't match
- All leaf diseases (NLB, Tar Spot, Common Rust, Gray Leaf Spot, Southern Rust, Stewart's, Goss's Wilt): Leaf symptoms — clearly don't match the ear rot

**Conclusion:** The pink/reddish mold color starting from the tip, combined with the overall progression pattern and the pinkish staining visible on the surrounding tissue, most closely match Gibberella ear rot. Gibberella (caused by *Fusarium graminearum*) characteristically shows pink-red mold progressing from the ear tip downward.
